description: Minerals are naturally occurring homogeneous solids with a definite chemical composition. In geography and economics, they are broadly classified into metallic and non-metallic categories based on their physical properties, chemical composition, and industrial applications.

sections.title: Classification of Minerals
sections.description: Minerals are categorized into different groups based on their characteristics, metal content, and usability.

key_concepts.explanation: Minerals that contain metal in raw form. They can be melted (smelted) to extract new metals and are generally good conductors of heat and electricity (e.g., Iron ore, Copper, Gold).
Minerals that do not contain extractable metals. They cannot be melted to yield new products and are usually poor conductors of heat and electricity (e.g., Mica, Limestone, Gypsum).

A sub-category of metallic minerals that contain iron. They account for about three-fourths of the total value of the production of metallic minerals and provide a strong base for metallurgical industries (e.g., Iron ore, Manganese).
Metallic minerals that do not contain iron. They play a vital role in a number of metallurgical, engineering, and electrical industries (e.g., Bauxite, Copper, Lead, Zinc).

sections.title: Major Ferrous Metallic Minerals
sections.description: Crucial iron-containing minerals that form the backbone of India's heavy industrial development.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Magnetite is the finest quality ore with a very high iron content (up to 70%). Hematite is the most important industrial iron ore with a slightly lower iron content (50-60%).
Mainly used in the manufacturing of steel and ferro-manganese alloys. It is also utilized in manufacturing bleaching powder, insecticides, and paints.

important_facts.fact: Odisha is the largest producer of iron ore in India, famous for its Badampahar mines in the Mayurbhanj and Kendujhar districts.
Madhya Pradesh is the leading producer of manganese in India, accounting for nearly one-third of the country's total production.

sections.title: Major Non-Ferrous Metallic Minerals
sections.description: Essential metallic minerals without iron content, highly demanded in the electrical, chemical, and technology sectors.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the chief ore used to produce alumina and subsequently aluminium. Aluminium is highly valued for its extreme lightness, good conductivity, and great malleability.
Being malleable, ductile, and a good conductor, it is mainly used in electrical cables, electronics, and chemical industries.

key_associations.extra_info: Historically significant mines located in the Jhunjhunu district, famous for copper extraction since the Indus Valley Civilization.
Once one of the deepest gold mines in the world, making mining highly expensive; currently non-operational.
Located in the Udaipur district, it is one of the oldest and most prominent lead-zinc producing regions in India.

sections.title: Major Non-Metallic Minerals
sections.description: Minerals lacking metallic properties that are indispensable for construction, energy, and electrical insulation.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Known for its excellent dielectric strength, low power loss factor, and insulating properties. It is an indispensable mineral used in electric and electronic industries.
Composed of calcium carbonate, it is the basic raw material for the cement industry and is essential for smelting iron ore in a blast furnace.

important_facts.fact: The Nellore district in Andhra Pradesh is world-famous for its high-quality mica production.
India is considered one of the world's largest producers and exporters of sheet mica.

sections.title: Scientific and Geographical Facts
sections.description: Important scientific principles related to mineral properties and key geographical facts about mineral distribution in India.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: A qualitative ordinal scale ranging from 1 to 10 that characterizes scratch resistance of various minerals.
scientific_principles.application: Talc is the softest mineral with a rating of 1, while Diamond is the hardest natural mineral with a rating of 10.

important_facts.fact: The Chhota Nagpur Plateau is often referred to as the 'Mineral Heartland of India' due to its massive and diverse concentration of mineral resources.
Uranium, a strategic nuclear mineral, is predominantly mined in Jaduguda, located in the Singhbhum district of Jharkhand.
Thorium, another critical nuclear fuel resource, is found in abundance in the monazite sands of the Kerala coast.
